instructions: Fill a large pot with water, add 2 tsp of the salt and bring it to a boil over high heat.
Thinly slice the onion and the fennel bulb. Chop 1/4 cup of the green fennel fronds and set them aside. Chop the garlic and the 4 anchovy fillets.
Toast 1/4 cup pine nuts in a large dry skillet over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring often, until golden and toasty. Transfer them to a small bowl.
Add the olive oil to the skillet over medium heat. Add the onion, the sliced fennel and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Cook for 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onion is soft and see-through.
As soon as the onion and fennel are in the pan, add the bucatini to the boiling water. Cook for 10 minutes, or as the box says, until it's tender with a little bite.
Add the anchovies to the skillet. Stir for 1 minute, until they melt into the oil.
Add the garlic, the saffron and the red pepper flakes. Stir for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant.
Add the wine and the raisins. Simmer for 3 minutes, until the wine is nearly gone.
Scoop out 1 cup of the pasta water, then drain the bucatini.
Drain the sardines and break them into big chunks. Add them to the skillet and stir gently for 1 minute, until they're warm.
Add the bucatini, 1/2 cup of the pasta water and the pine nuts. Toss for 1 minute, until the sauce clings. Add more pasta water if it looks dry.
Take the skillet off the heat. Stir in the chopped fennel fronds.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: No version had 20 ratings, so the lead (Pamela Salzman, 5 stars from 2 ratings) is the first one read. It cooks onion and fennel, adds garlic, wine and currants, then warms the sardines and tosses everything with bucatini. Food Network Kitchen has the same base plus saffron, anchovy and toasted crumbs, which is the more Sicilian version. This takes the saffron and anchovy from the Food Network version, drops the crumbs to stay near 30 minutes, and cuts the sardines to 2 tins for 12 oz of pasta. It comes in a little over 30 minutes at 32.
